To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current knowledge is insufficient to recommend the systematic screening for prostatic cancer, but the debate on the subject must not be closed.
the current data of the published literature are insufficient to define a screening policy for prostatic cancer.

1) the current data do not allow us to conclude on the impact of PSA mass screening on the morbity and mortality of prostate cancer; 2) the absence of proof of the favourable impact of screening does not mean that it is useless.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) Is prostatic cancer a disease which justifies screening?
the following questions: Is it possible to define a population at risk of prostatic cancer?
the following questions: 1) Does screening for prostatic cancer by serum PSA assay reduce the mortality due to this disease?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of a randomized prospective study, the current data do not permit us to define a screening policy for prostatic cancer.
1) PSA screening should not be performed in the general population.
PSA-based screening is not recommended, and that PSA should only be used in the context of a clinical suspicion of prostatic cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current knowledge does not allow us to recommend or to condemn the PSA screening policy.
, in the absence of a randomized study, it is not possible to recommend or not to recommend prostatic cancer screening by serum PSA.

1) the screening policy must be reconsidered; 2) the screening policy should not be based on a single test; 3) the screening policy cannot be based on a simple PSA assay; 4) the screening policy requires a combination of PSA assay, digital rectal examination and prostate ultrasound; 5) the screening policy can only be proposed to men with a life-expectancy of more than 15 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at present, there is no justification for a systematic PSA screening policy.
, in the current state of our knowledge, PSA screening should be discouraged.
the screening of prostatic cancer by PSA assay must be the subject of randomized prospective studies.
